summary: Dominant defects: (1) the rule 'link to a facet stays with the entity' is applied unevenly (application_constraint stays, but model_secret_backend, model_authorized_keys, model_last_login, application_resource, annotation_* go the other way), so the one-home rule fails for every noun-noun link table (machine_volume, storage_attachment, application_endpoint, unit_resource, offer_connection, relation_network_egress). (2) Pages that are two things: model-migration (source export vs target import), offer (offering vs consuming side), storage (user-facing vs provisioning), controller (singleton vs HA nodes), agent-version (target version vs binary index), plus CAAS-only objects scattered over application and unit. (3) Misplaced: model_namespace, model_database_deletion (database); flag (controller bootstrap); bakery_config and macaroon_root_key (not user); block_device and block_device_link_device (machine). (4) One thing: space+subnet+zone (single domain/network and SubnetInfo carries zones), user+permission (domain/access), port into unit, status page empty. (5) Lookups: secret_backend_origin is secret-backend's; workload_status_value is shared; duplicated storage status lists. (6) Controller and model schemas both define object_store_metadata, agent_binary_store, model, change_log, life, architecture, password_hash_algorithm, ssh_key_algorithm_type; the proposal lacks a database qualifier. Caveat: ownership counts come from string matching of FROM/INTO/JOIN in non-test domain Go code; the model_constraint and application_remote_offerer_relation_macaroon entries in misplaced are cautions, not moves.
